transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just done your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can actually start light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you'll want to avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's helpful to know. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

If you don't have any at the moment, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I have noticed that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, that is quite normal actually. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside. However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, I'll keep an eye on it. I do have one more question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long ago you had your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after the operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago did you have your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I had the surgery about a week ago. I'll keep monitoring the blurriness like you suggested. Thanks for answering all my questions, Dora! I don't have any more at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and don't hesitate to get in touch if you have any concerns during your recovery.

verdict.label: pass

Finally, Dora completes the turn by saying, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further," which covers `escalation_criteria`.
